bill.title: Ending Improper Payments to Deceased People Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 371.
bill.officialSummary: Ending Improper Payments to Deceased People Act This bill permanently allows the Department of the Treasury to access certain death records maintained by the Social Security Administration (SSA) in order to facilitate the identification and prevention of improper payments (e.g., payments to deceased individuals). Current law requires the SSA to share its Death Master File with the Do Not Pay system maintained by Treasury for three years. The bill makes this requirement permanent.

classification.plainSummary: This bill makes permanent a requirement that the Social Security Administration share its death records with the Treasury Department's Do Not Pay system. Currently, this data-sharing arrangement is authorized for only three years at a time. The goal is to help federal agencies identify and stop payments mistakenly sent to people who have died.

plain.whatItDoes: This bill permanently would allow the Treasury Department to access certain death records maintained by the Social Security Administration to facilitate the identification and prevention of improper payments (e.g., payments to deceased people).
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in your monthly payment. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.
plain.source: Reworded from the official summary. Staff at the Congressional Research Service wrote that summary. It is public domain, and the full text of it is further down this page.
